live_issue.title: [v0.92.1][Runtime] Support TLS 1.2 on public Axum HTTPS/WSS for Unity
live_issue.body:
## Problem

Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener is hard-coded to TLS 1.3 only. Unity 6000.5.1f1's UnityTLS client negotiates TLS 1.2 with otherwise compatible public endpoints and cannot complete the Runtime handshake. This blocks issue #84 even with a valid CA-issued certificate and complete Let’s Encrypt chain.

The restriction is currently explicit in `adl-runtime-kernel/src/tls.rs` through `with_protocol_versions(&[&rustls::version::TLS13])`.

## Diagnostic evidence

The #84 native Unity Play Mode lane established the following controls:

- Unity accepted Let’s Encrypt's official X2-terminating Gen-Y test endpoint.
- Unity rejected direct Root YE trust, as expected.
- A separately issued short-lived ECDSA Wuji leaf with the same YE/X2 certificate shape still failed against the ADL Runtime with UnityTLS error code 7.
- The exact Wuji short-lived leaf and chain succeeded when served by OpenSSL on the same host and port. Unity negotiated TLS 1.2 and advanced past certificate validation to the expected application-layer timeout.
- Therefore the certificate, hostname, ECDSA key, and X2 chain are not the blocker; the Runtime's TLS 1.3-only public listener is the discriminating boundary.

Retained local evidence in the #84 worktree includes:

- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T063900Z-live.log` — official X2 endpoint accepted at TLS layer.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064625Z-live.log` — short-lived Wuji certificate rejected against Runtime.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064949Z-live.log` — identical Wuji certificate presentation accepted through OpenSSL; application layer intentionally non-Runtime.

## Required outcome

Support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 on Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener using the shared reviewed Rustls provider and secure ECDHE cipher suites, while preserving TLS 1.3-only behavior for Quinn Guardian transport where that is a protocol invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- Public Axum HTTPS/WSS server configuration enables both Rustls TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
- TLS 1.2 support is limited to reviewed forward-secret AEAD suites compatible with the configured ECDSA and RSA certificate policies; no legacy TLS versions or weak suites are enabled.
- Quinn Guardian mTLS remains TLS 1.3-only unless a separate reviewed requirement changes it.
- Focused tests prove the public listener accepts TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 and rejects TLS 1.1 and earlier.
- Focused tests cover CA-issued ECDSA identity loading and complete-chain presentation without leaf-as-root trust.
- The real Unity 6000.5.1f1 Play Mode product adapter completes HTTPS and WSS authentication against the Runtime without a proxy, trust-store mutation, custom always-accept certificate handler, or verification bypass.
- Existing browser/curl clients continue to negotiate TLS 1.3 when supported.
- Runtime startup remains fail-closed for invalid identity, incomplete chain, wrong SAN, expiry, unsuitable EKU, and unknown issuer.
- Observability records negotiated TLS version without logging credentials or certificate private material.

## Non-goals

- Disabling certificate validation or adding a Unity-specific trust bypass.
- Installing or mutating host keychain trust.
- Adding a TLS-termination proxy as the product solution.
- Weakening Quinn Guardian mutual authentication.
- Reissuing certificates as a substitute for protocol compatibility.
- Implementing this change inside issue #84.

## Issue graph

- Follow-up to closed TLS standardization issue #92.
- Blocks the real native Unity acceptance lane and publication of #84.
- #84 owns only the Unity consumer and must treat this Runtime change as an upstream dependency.
